nt`: the client's hosted\n model selection carries `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the runner applies it\n (and refuses a model
that cannot) — see [`HostRunner`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/host-runner#reasoningeffort).\n* Build the runner yourself
with `HostRunner({ reasoningEffort })`.\n* Set the effort on the hosted suite's model selection with\n `mcpjam cloud eval update

--effort <level>` (see the [CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#reasoning-effort)).

## Tool policy

A su
ite's `defaults.toolPolicy` is enforced before the MCP call: a denied tool never reaches the server, the model receives the refusa
l, and the report records the block by case, iteration and call id. A blocked call is not graded as a call and is not an executed
tool span. A `deny` name that matches no tool the servers expose is invalid input (exit `2`); an unmatched `allow` is a warning. W

ith no `toolPolicy`, nothing is restrained.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For the upcoming Inspector eval runner with MCP App view tools enab
led, use `view:<name>` in a suite's `toolPolicy.allow` or `deny`, for example `view:make_move`. These names wait until the app ren
ders; plain tool names keep the validation described above. Assertions and side-effect manifests still use `make_move`. This synta

x does not enable view tools in the local SDK suite-file runner.

## Imported cases

Native and claimed-`exact` imported cases
run with no approval. An `approximated` case runs only when this invocation approves it:\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variab
les\"}\nmcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/imported.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \\\n --approval-reason \"Reviewed aga

inst the upstream rubric"
```

`unsupported` and `unresolved` cases never run. Approving a native, `exact`, disabled, unselect
ed or unknown case is refused. A local approval is recorded as local evidence; it claims no hosted approver.\n\n## What runs local

ly

| Capability | Local behavior |
| - | - |
| Prompt steps (including several per case) | Run as one conversation per iterat
ion |\n| Deterministic assertions (steps and `assertions`) | Graded with the hosted assertion engine |\n| Direct `toolCall` steps
| Refused before anything runs — use a prompt, or run hosted |\n| `interact` steps, widget/render and tool-discovery assertions |
Refused before anything runs |\n| Gating assertions on tool results or per-call latency (`toolResultContains`, `toolResultMatches`
, `toolResultMatchesSchema`, `toolResultSizeUnder`, `toolLatencyUnder`) | Refused before anything runs — a local run does not capt
ure tool results or timings yet. An advisory one is reported as not measured |\n| An enabled gating or required judge | Refused be
fore anything runs |\n| An advisory judge (including the hosted default) | Not run; the report says so |\n| `suppressedSuiteStanda
rdCheckIds` | Refused — a local run has no suite-standard registry |\n\nEvery selected case is checked before any model or tool ca
ll, so an unsupported later case costs nothing. Hosted-only capabilities run with `mcpjam cloud eval run --file <file>`.\n\n## Out
put\n\n* With `--format human` (the default on a terminal), a summary: the verdict, each case's gradeable-iteration count against
its threshold, failing assertions, not-measured iterations, policy blocks and un-run judges.\n* With `--format json` (the default
when stdout is not a terminal: a pipe, a CI log, or an agent's shell), one JSON report on stdout (`kind: \"eval-local-run\"`). Pas
s `--format human` to get the summary there instead.\n* `--reporter json-summary|junit-xml|html` writes that document to stdout; t
he human summary and progress go to stderr.\n* `--out <path>` writes the report atomically (in the `--reporter` format, else JSON)
and prints the path.\n\nEvery report identifies the run as local and emulated, carries the source-file sha256, the per-case evalu
ator hashes, the selection, the effective model and rail per case and each server's binding source, and states that upload was off
. Server headers, environment objects, command lines and token-bearing URLs never appear in any output, and every credential the r
un was given is redacted wherever observed text (an error, a tool argument) repeats it.\n\nThe unit of a verdict is the **case**;
iterations are evidence. A JUnit consumer receives a `<failure>` only for a measured failure — provider errors, evaluator errors a

nd interrupted work are reported as skipped, never as failed assertions.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0`
| The run completed and its decision passed |\n| `1` | The run completed and its decision failed — the only source of `1` |\n| `2`
| Invalid file or flags, an unsupported local capability, an import/approval refusal, or an invalid tool-policy deny name |\n| `3
` | Missing or rejected model or platform credentials, including during execution |\n| `4` | Setup, connection, tool catalog, bind
ing, interpolation or billing failure, or a report that could not be written |\n| `5` | Inconclusive, interrupted, an integrity fa
ilure, or no complete verdict |\n\n`Ctrl-C` stops the run cooperatively: completed evidence is kept, the report is written, and th
e command exits `5` — an interrupted run is never presented as a completed release gate. A second `Ctrl-C` exits immediately.\n\n#
# From code\n\nThe same engine is `runSuiteFile` in `@mcpjam/sdk`. It takes explicit bindings and credentials — it reads no files,
environment or login store — and returns the decision and the report. See [runSuiteFile](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/ru

n-suite-file.md).
